text.insert: Initial Sync turns the configured checkout and captured sources into accepted build evidence and searchable knowledge. Sandbox validation then proves that the selected worker image can reproduce the accepted host build. Run starts only after its required readiness gates succeed.

steps.text: Validate identity, repository, target/build profile, tools, and declared external sources.
Report missing required credentials or capabilities without treating missing data as an empty source.
Provision the configured checkout before initial Sync; resolve and verify its Git source identity.
Build and validate the selected target; derive report targets and source entities before curation.
Capture initial PR, Discord, and wiki material according to declared scope.
Import immutable records and build search indexes.
Queue or run librarian backfill; record which subjects and source captures were covered.
Run validate-sandbox for the selected profile after initial Sync accepts build evidence.
Build host and Daytona reports at the accepted head; compare scored functions and sizes and preserve proof.
Require the configured bootstrap gates, with optional unfinished curation visibly pending.
Persist accepted head, upstream baseline, configuration provenance, and initial save point.
Enable Run admission only after readiness succeeds. Resume interrupted setup from durable stage results.

text.insert: Bootstrap requires declared source acquisition, import, and search indexes, plus mechanical entities and valid build evidence. Semantic curation can remain pending with visible coverage. Sandbox readiness requires separate verified execution evidence before Run admission.

Initial Sync accepts the configured checkout and build evidence before sandbox validation. The validation command reserves exclusive dispatch authority, checks the accepted head and configuration, builds host and Daytona reports, compares scored functions and sizes, preserves evidence, and deletes the sandbox. Only successful validation marks sandbox readiness ready. Initial readiness is recorded when every required gate is ready.
Evidence lives under the resolved game state directory at

. It records host and remote reports, profile, image, accepted head, configuration, and build output. This operation contacts Daytona. Configuration tests alone do not satisfy the gate, and no live validation is implied by a registered descriptor.

Harness State owns the canonical worktree and source lineage. Sync owns upstream intake, staging, validation, and confirmed publication. Descriptor resolution alone does not establish bootstrap readiness.
